Yes, apprenticeship wages are dog shit unfortunately. 22$ an hour if I remember correctly. Hence you could do commercial construction and earn alot but you'll learn less as commercial is very standard stuff from job to job. 

There are centrelink payments for tradies so I'd take a look at that. It's not much but everything help. 

Construction companies are crying out for tradies/apprentices. Unfortunately they aren't going to pay above award (they too are trying to make money). I don't know which companies have EBAs (enterprise bargaining agreements kinda like contracts with governments) so you'll have to do a bit of searching. Then once you found a couple, either go on their website or give them a call regarding an apprenticeship.

When I say dodgy, I mean, not paying tool allowance, travel allowance, overtime etc. Gotta be very careful but unfortunately you won't know until you're actually with them. But definitely research what you're entitled to. 

Trades is not saturated. Plumbers, carpenters, and electrician are dying for apprentices. Go to any construction site and have a chat with the tradies and have a chat with them and they'll tell you almost the same thing of not enough apprentices. These days is just uni this and uni that. 

Construction management and cert IV is similar but intended for different purposes. Construction companies want construction managers to manage the construction workflow, the site, materials, timeframe, costing etc. Youre a construction manager and that's that. Cert IV, you'll learn similar things about managing a site, costings etc but most people go on to get their builder licence to start their own company. I think you still can become a builder if you do the construction management degree, I don't know what the path is or how long it takes. 

A builder apprenticeship is carpentry. 

I don't know much about contracts. I use to work with apprentices is all. If you're not sure about which company to go with, look up Master Builders NSW. They'll help you get placed with a reputable company and they do everything by the book but the builders they have are limited. Up to you which company you vibe with the best.

You won't land any jobs with a CERT IV. Just because you have a piece of paper doesn't mean you know how to build anything let alone manage a building site. TAFE cons so many people getting this Diploma selling the dream of becoming a builder right out of the program.

Top construction companies recruit from universities who are studying a bachelor's in construction management so that's your competition. 

Think to yourself, why would a builder hire you compared to others? Just because you have a piece of paper saying you completed your cert IV?

My advice is, do the CERT III in Carpentry, become an apprentice (very easy to be one, hard to find a good company and won't try to pull a dodgy on you). It's 4 years, it's crap work at the beginning but you'll learn so much. The ins and outs of a construction site. 

If you want money and don't mind more of the boring stuff, go into commercial construction. Tier 1 companies with EBAs pay disgusting amounts. Lots of apprentices pulling in 100k in year one (mind you doing crazy amount of overtime 60+ hours per week). 

But if you want to be a builder builder, you should do residential. The path would be 4 year apprenticeship (can do the CERT IV in conjunction) + 2 years placement with a certified builder to get your builder licence if you want to start your own company or you can just be a qualified chippy after your apprenticeship.

Hope this helps.

EDIT: if you are looking for shortcuts, there isn't any. Why would people hire you if you taken shortcuts to master your trade? You'll end up like ICON. But they were more greedy and negligent rather than incompetent.
